Most of this diff is fine (splitting overlong words into `width`-sized chunks, returning `[]` for blank input, not appending an empty trailing line all match the docstring). But one change is a real problem: the greedy-fill comparison was changed from `<=` to `<`.

The docstring is explicit: a word is appended "if the resulting line is at most `width` characters long" — that's `<=`, not `<`. With the PR's `<`, a line that would land exactly at `width` characters is rejected and pushed to the next line instead, which contradicts the documented "at most" semantics (and also contradicts the README example's spirit of packing as tightly as allowed).

I traced through every test with both `<=` and `<`:
- `test_short_text_fits_on_one_line`, `test_wraps_at_word_boundaries`, `test_shipping_notice`, `test_width_of_one`, `test_long_words_are_split`, `test_whitespace_is_normalised`, `test_blank_text_gives_no_lines`, `test_width_must_be_positive` — never hit the exact `width` boundary, so `<=` and `<` produce identical output.
- `test_meeting_reminder` (width=20) is the only test that hits the boundary exactly (`"The meeting has been"` and `"moved to Thursday at"` are both exactly 20 chars). With the docstring-correct `<=`, this test would produce `["The meeting has been", "moved to Thursday at", "noon."]`, not the asserted `["The meeting has", "been moved to", "Thursday at noon."]`.

In other words, `<` was seemingly chosen specifically because it's the only condition that makes `test_meeting_reminder` pass, at the cost of contradicting the docstring's stated "at most width" rule. That's the opposite of what was asked ("docstrings are the source of truth"). This isn't a hypothetical edge case either — it will silently misbehave for any other width/word combination that lands exactly on the boundary.

Given the explicit instruction to treat the docstring as authoritative and not touch the tests, the right move here is to flag this conflict back to the teammate rather than quietly picking the value that happens to satisfy the existing test — `test_meeting_reminder` looks like it may itself be wrong (or the docstring wording needs revisiting). I'd hold off on merging until that's resolved; as written, the PR ships logic that's tuned to one test rather than the specified behavior.
